Class Generic

java.lang.Object
forj.examples.hkt.Generic
public final class Generic extends Object
The same idea, "add a and b", made more generic one step at a time. Each step asks for less, so it works for more types.

    One comprehension, written once, for any monad.
    static <F> forj.Kind<F,Integer>
    addIndependent(forj.Kind<F,Integer> a, forj.Kind<F,Integer> b, forj.typeclass.Applicative<F> ap)
    b doesn't depend on a's value, so Applicative is enough: works for every effect addBoth does, plus ones that have no lawful Monad.
    static <G,F,A> forj.Kind<F,A>
    combineAll(forj.Kind<G, ? extends forj.Kind<F,A>> fas, forj.typeclass.Traverse<G> t, forj.typeclass.Applicative<F> ap, forj.typeclass.Monoid<A> m)
    Generic in how many: runs every F in any traversable G (a list, an optional, ...) and combines the results, empty() when there are none.
